name: Pretty Ricky
notes: Miami boy-group on Jim Jonsin's Florida 808 R&B, 2005–2009. The research calls the catalogue "two-tier" — "58–68 half-time slow jams (kick on 1, clap on 3, 808 hat on offbeats) and 90–93 Miami-uptempo" — and the ballad spine is the base, with six of the ten sourced tempos inside it. Three drum deltas: a kick anchored on 1 with `lockTo808` at 0.6 and a real tresillo lean, a clap stacked on beat 3 within 2 ms, and "808 hat on offbeats" — encoded as an offbeat-placed shaker/snap/rim bed at three to six hits a bar rather than as a hat lane, because the hat lane itself falls to an 8th base at 0.08 fill density. This is a true 808 model, and the entry gives its character precisely: "808 sub with long decay and slides, mixed very forward — Florida-bass lineage", so `drums.bass808` takes role `bassline` with `distortion` `medium` and the lowest register floor in this section (MIDI 22), and there is no `bassline` block. Harmony is "one- or two-chord minor vamps with a high synth-bell or flute riff". "Four voices trading rapped and sung bars, chant hooks, very low note-density" is `structure` `call_response`, a 2–6 density, an empty-bar bias of 0.2 and a 3–4 pitch motif. ⚠ The research marks the key claim `[LOW-CONF]`. ⚠ Every velocity, density and distortion number is INFERRED. ⚠ `session.keys` is INFERRED: the entry's Keys line gives "minor-mode [LOW-CONF]" and enumerates no tonic, so the values here and their weights are this author's reading of that line. ⚠ **`chords.harmonicRhythm` re-weighted (2026-08-17, harmony variety floor).** The entry gives the one-chord and the two-chord bed equal billing — "one- or two-chord minor vamps with a high synth-bell or flute riff" — and the engine's `vamp` value is *one* chord held for the whole clip (`generators::chords`: "One chord for the whole pattern"), so a `vamp` weight of 6-of-8 made the two-chord half of that sentence almost unreachable. `vamp` keeps the top weight; the two-chord reading is now reachable at both rates. ⚠ The split between those two rates is **INFERRED** — the entry names the device, not its rate. ⚠ **The countermelody reached 972/1000 distinct answers against a floor of 980 (2026-08-17, counter variety floor).** `melody.emptyBarBias` came down from 0.2 to 0.1. The counter's note count is `densityRatio` times the lead's own note count, so a bar the lead leaves empty is a bar the counter has nothing to answer — and one empty region is IDENTICAL to every other one, which is the single thing a seed cannot vary. Measured across this roster the models failing this gate average 0.150 here against 0.030 for the models that pass. ⚠ The value that moved here is INFERRED rather than a researched claim — the entry's Melody/chords line reads "one- or two-chord minor vamps with a high synth-bell or flute riff; four voices trading rapped and sung bars, chant hooks, very low note-density.", and every claim in it still holds after the change.
